text:
morgan: Proposal — introduce probabilistic backoff + a confidence score for paging GPU-critical alerts. Goal: cut noisy pages while preserving rapid escalation for high-confidence incidents. Want quick feedback before I draft PR.

alex: +1 idea. What signals feed the confidence score?

morgan: Metrics: `node_gpu_utilization`, `pod_eviction_rate`, `node_restarts_total`, `kv_cache_miss_rate`. Idea: compute an anomaly score per node (EWMA of z-score over 1m/5m), then aggregate to cluster-level confidence = weighted sum (recurrence, severity, topology-spread). Simple policy: conf < 0.6 -> create ticket only; 0.6-0.85 -> probabilistic page with backoff; >0.85 -> immediate page. Group by cluster/region/gpu_type.

sophie: Can you paste PromQL and an example alert rule? Also need Alertmanager routing changes.

morgan: Sure — rough PromQL and rule sketch: 
```promql
# per-node anomaly (pseudo)
node_gpu_anom = (node_gpu_utilization - avg_over_time(node_gpu_utilization[1h])) / stddev_over_time(node_gpu_utilization[1h])
node_anom_ewma = ewma(node_gpu_anom[1m], 0.3)
# cluster confidence = recency * spread factor * severity
cluster_conf = sum(node_anom_ewma * on(node) label_replace(node_labels, "gpu_type", "$1", "node", "(.+)") ) / count(node_anom_ewma)
```
And an alert rule sketch (yaml):
```yaml
- alert: GPUClusterDegradation
  expr: cluster_conf > 1.2
  labels:
    severity: critical
    pager_confidence: "{{ $labels.cluster_conf }}"
  annotations:
    summary: "GPU cluster {{ $labels.cluster }} high anomaly score"
    runbook: ">> runbook link <<"
    prob_page: "true"
```
Note: `prob_page` will be used by a small routing layer to decide whether to page immediately or run the backoff logic.

devon: How do we implement the probabilistic backoff? I worry about under-notifying when multiple correlated nodes are failing.

morgan: Backoff plan: when 0.6<=conf<0.85, compute page_probability = sigmoid((conf-0.6)/0.1) clamped to [0.3,0.9]. Then:
- sample once per alert evaluation window (1m). If sample passes -> page group (with grouping by cluster+region+gpu_type).
- keep a burst_budget per cluster (tokens replenish slowly) so we don't flood on transient spikes.
- if alert persists > 15m OR affects >X% of nodes -> bypass sampling and page immediately.

jamie: Nice. Proposal for rollout + observability:
- Create a canary channel (eng-sre-canary) and enable probabilistic paging for 5% of clusters for 2 weeks.
- Build a Grafana board: paging-rate-by-confidence, tickets-created-vs-pages, mean-time-to-ack by conf-bin.
- Add SLO guard: if pages_to_incidents ratio drops > 30% for high-sev alerts -> auto-rollback.

sophie: Alertmanager side: we can add a webhook receiver that reads `pager_confidence` + `prob_page` and returns `page` or `ticket` action. I can mock the webhook and a simple feature-flag toggle.

devon: Edge cases: network partition in a region could make confidence low (because metrics delayed). Suggest we include a freshness check: if scrape_delay > 30s mark confidence_multipler = 1.2 (more likely to page) to avoid false negatives. Also add a check against `region_slo_impact` metric to force page when product metrics degrade.

morgan: Good call on freshness. We'll add `metric_freshness_ok` boolean into the scoring and `region_slo_impact` as an override.

ops-bot: scheduled: load-test/simulate-probabilistic-backoff-run at 2025-11-10T15:00Z (reminder posted)

alex: For the PR let's include: Prometheus rule, small evaluator service (stateless, runs alongside alertmanager), feature-flag, canary list, dashboards, and a rollback playbook.

morgan: I'll draft the PR with the rule + evaluator + dashboards. Assigning to @sophie for webhook + @jamie for canary dashboard. Will ping when ready. :thumbsup:

sophie: ack, will prototype webhook this week.

jamie: I'll sketch the dashboard and SLO checks.

devon: I'll update the runbook with the bypass criteria and example troubleshooting steps (commands to check node metrics and groupings).

morgan: Thanks all — aim to have the PR by EOD Friday. If anyone objects to the approach please raise here.
